He helped coordinate relief efforts for Jewish communities devastated by the fighting and worked to secure minority rights under the new Polish state. In 1919, Reich was elected to the constituent assembly of the short-lived West Ukrainian People's Republic, though his primary focus remained on Jewish communal autonomy.

Throughout the interwar period, he continued to play a prominent role in Polish Jewish politics. He advocated for Jewish cultural and educational institutions while pressing the government in Warsaw to honor its minority protection obligations. Reich also maintained his Zionist commitments, helping to strengthen the movement's organizational infrastructure across Galicia. He wrote extensively on Jewish political questions and contributed to numerous Yiddish and Hebrew publications. His leadership made him one of the most influential figures in Eastern European Jewish public life during the turbulent interwar years.

pair.human_continuation:
When the Polish–Ukrainian War broke out, he was interned by Polish authorities at a camp in Baranów. He was released with intervention from Józef Piłsudski, Naḥum Sokolow, and Western European Jewish leaders. During the Paris Peace Conference, he was vice-president of the Comité des Délégations Juives and edited a book on the national rights of Eastern European Jews called Les droits nationaux des Juifs en Europe orientale (The National Rights of Jews in Western Europe) in 1919. He wrote a memoir of that period in 1922 called Żydowska delegacja pokojowa w Paryżu (The Jewish Peace Delegation in Paris).

Reich practiced law in Lviv. In 1920, he became chairman of the Zionist Organization of Eastern Galicia. In the 1922 Polish legislative election, he was elected to the Sejm.
pair.prefix:
In 1913, he represented Eastern Galician Zionists on the executive committee of the Zionist Organization. He took part in the Zionist Congresses as a leading delegate of the General Zionists. He edited a Polish Zionist in 1910. In the 1911 election, he unsuccessfully ran for the Imperial Council.

During World War I, Reich served in the legal department of the Austro-Hungarian Army. After the war, he was a main organizer of the Jewish National Council of East Galicia.
